_comment: When the Bitwarden machine-account token in BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN stops working.
NO SECRET IS IN THIS FILE. A BWS access token carries no expiry inside it --
expiry is a property of the machine account, held server-side and visible only
in the web vault. So the date has to be written down by whoever minted the
token, and the only alternative is discovering it when every local command
starts failing with an opaque auth error.
That is not hypothetical: mc_migrate_claude was minted 2026-09-01 with 7-day
validity, and agent/PLAN-env-to-bitwarden.md would have every local script
depend on it. Silence here becomes a scheduled outage.
Update this whenever a token is minted or replaced. `warn_days` is how long
before the date the tools start shouting.
client_id_sha256 fingerprints the IDENTIFIER half of the token, never the secret.
It exists so a token swapped without updating this file is reported, rather than
the date silently describing a machine account that no longer exists.
replacement_plan: agent/PLAN-env-to-bitwarden.md -- split into mc-ci-read (read-only, lives in .env) and mc-rotate (read-write, supplied per rotation, never stored)
